newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Q1 exports up 3 pct yr/yr-Commerce Ministry.
newsitem.headline: Thai Q1 exports up 3 pct yr/yr-Commerce Ministry.

text.p: The Thai commerce ministry said on Monday exports rose 3.0 percent in the first quarter to 365.42 billion baht ($14.05 billion) over the year-ago period.
It said exports grew eight percent in the same period last year to 354.9 billion baht.
The ministry said imports in the quarter fell 3.4 percent to 452.18 billion baht. In the first quarter of 1996, imports jumped 13.7 percent to a total of 467.99 billion baht.

The country's trade deficit in the first quarter totalled 86.76 billion baht, down 23.3 percent from the same quarter a year ago, it said. The trade deficit in the first three month in 1996 amounted to 113.09 billion baht.
The Bank of Thailand earlier said preliminary figures showed exports grew an average 4.4 percent in the first four months. It did not give a figure for the first quarter.

Trade figures differ from the commerce ministry and the Bank of Thailand as the agencies use different formulas for calculation. Concern over Thailand's sluggish export performance and ailing property sector have been dogging the country's stock and foreign exchange markets in the last few months.
Computer parts and electronic boards were the top export items in the quarter with a total export value of 44.19 billion baht and 16.45 billion baht respectively, the ministry said.
Thailand's major export markets were ASEAN countries and the United States with exports amounting to 73.94 billion baht and 58.27 billion baht, respectively, it said.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
